convoLines.text: "I hate to ask this, but I can't shake it. I'm feverish, a cut gone hot and angry. Can you do anything?"
"Rest won't touch this. The heat's climbing and my head's full of cotton. Someone who knows what they're doing — please."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"There's more, but that's for another fire."
"Werner owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
You show them Serviceberry — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Do you still sing? ...Sorry — weird question. I just realized I haven't heard anyone sing."
"Ha! The creek concerts. I've heard those. Keep going."
"Under my breath, when I'm working. Old songs from Columbus, Ohio. The words are half gone but the tune holds. Tunes outlast everything."
"...What's that supposed to mean?" Their voice goes careful.
"Still on whether you still sing."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
"You're a good listener, you know that?" A tired smile.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"Never mind the sickness I'm fighting — we got it handled. Thanks anyway."
They grin when they spot you — unguarded, for once.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "Werner always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"Nobody says Werner's name right yet. We will. Give it a few days."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Still on what's been happening."
You show them Pokeweed — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"This was good." They mean it.
"You've been singing in the creek. Badly, by your own admission. Heard anything worth stealing yet?"
"Come see what I found. You won't believe it."
Sophia shows you where they go to think. "Don't tell the others. Everyone needs one place."
Their eyes do the math before their mouth does. You can see the calculation happening.
A wall comes down, then — surprisingly — a door opens behind it. "I wasn't an EMT. I was a Rancher. You don't know what it's like, being the only nobody in a camp of somebodies." Quiet. Real.
"You're really going to make me say it again?" Sophia rubs their face. "Fine — but it's the same truth as last time."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"...I need to go be quiet for a while."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"We never finished talking about that foraging help — we wandered off it, 7 days back. 'Forget I said anything. What did you want?'"
"Take your time."

"It's my grandmother, Alina. Was taken. Eighty-one years old and they called her boring. Eighty-one years. Some nights I dream about the pods -- rows of them, humming. I wake up and I can't tell if it was a dream or a broadcast."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Duel. They just... took Ivy. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
"That's the whole of it. Sorry."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Hi. Sorry. I'm not good at the talking-to-strangers part."
Something eases in their shoulders. "Oh. Okay. That's... that's fine, then."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"As I said — Still on what's been happening."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
"Thanks for listening. Most people change the subject."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Oh — We never finished talking about that personal stuff — we left it mid-thought, 7 days back. 'A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.'"
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Still on that personal stuff."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Okay. That's — I need a minute. A long minute."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Good — that personal stuff, settled. Feels better said out loud."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Can I tell you something? I've been hiding an injury. I'm ashamed and I can't stop."
Their whole posture softens around you.
"Still on what they confided."
"...Anyway. What did you want to ask?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Last time things were different. They always are." "The Cache. They just... took Vasyl. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"Right. Go on, then."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
"This was good." They mean it.
"I keep dreaming about rows of pods. Humming. Tell me I'm not the only one."
"It's my sister, Niamh. Was taken at the Scattering. The boring half, they said — my sister, boring. I think about that every day. The pods get into my sleep some nights.
Row on row of them, humming like a held note -- and I wake up reaching for something that isn't there."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
The easy manner evaporates. What's left is watching you back.
A wall comes down, then — surprisingly — a door opens behind it. "I'm not from Denver. I'm from Columbus, Ohio. The truth felt small. The lie felt like someone worth keeping around." Quiet. Real.
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"Yeah. Sorry. It's -- never mind. Forget I said anything." They look away, embarrassed at having wanted something.
"Tell me — Still on that taken person."
"They're already drifting away. "Later."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Hey — I found some Pokeweed today. You were right, it was right where you said."
They light up a little when they see you.
"There's more, but that's for another fire."
"Still on that plant lesson."
"Yeah? What's up?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Everyone's choosing sides and pretending they aren't. I hate it."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"You talk to it -- the System. Have you ever asked? About the taken -- about Niamh?"
"All right. Thank you for telling me."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"Still nothing on Niamh. I told you about the pods -- I keep thinking about them. The humming. Some nights I'm sure it's a dream. Other nights I'm sure it's not."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"You feel that? The air before a storm. That's the village right now."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
You show them Serviceberry — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"...I need to go be quiet for a while."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Thanks for listening. Most people change the subject."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to that taken person."
"This was good." They mean it.
"I'm sorry — I can't shake it. I'm achy and wrung out, barely keeping food down. I need help. Please."
"Rest and clean water aren't cutting it. If this turns, I'm no good to anyone — can't haul, can't hunt, can't watch. I need someone who knows what they're doing."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"We lost Kelly and Liam this week. I keep setting out extra portions. Stupid."
"Yes. Absolutely. I've been hoping you'd ask." (A little too quickly.)
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
They speak. You understand none of it.
They answer at length. They nod back, slowly.
They answer at length. A grin breaks through, quick and warm. "You good?"
They answer at length. You tap your chest, then theirs. Us. They nod, emphatic.
A final shared look — you both feel the talk running its course.
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Between us — I keep expecting to see them by the fire. Then I remember."
"Come get air with me. I need to think out loud."
Sam has been stockpiling where nobody looks. "Take half. You've got the hands for it." (+4 wood, +4 fiber to the village stash.)
"Performance Review — A red line draws itself across the ground. It hunts by day — watch the open ground."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"Thanks. ...Thanks for saying that. ...sorry."
"Sophia is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
You show them Serviceberry — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"I keep turning over the last thing Sophia said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Right. Go on, then."
"Thanks for... you know. Just listening."
"This was good." They mean it.
They spread their hands, smiling — the words are missing, but the meaning lands anyway.
"Sure — what's on your mind?"
A gesture, patient and clear: palms up, then toward you.
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
A warmth settles over the conversation — they lean in a little.
They answer at length. A grin breaks through, quick and warm.
They glance toward their own thoughts; the exchange is winding down.
"This was good." They mean it.

deathBeat: d41: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Werner Ding is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d41: 🕯️ Werner Ding is dead — a hushwolf. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d41: The village's quarrel was with Werner — and Werner is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
recoverHome: d42: That night, they bring Werner home. Nobody asks you to help carry; nobody has to. By morning the grave is dug by the fire, and the body is laid out beside it. The filling of it is yours.
vouch: d41: At the grave, Kelly, Sophia, Vasyl and 1 more speak for Ella — "Werner trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
systemVoice: d41: SYSTEM: Identification complete. You are 0.3% less lost.
d43: ◈ AUDIENCE TRIAL — SYSTEM: "The audience wants an encore. A trial, then — smaller this time, but televised." Haul 1,000 kcal to the pantry within 3 days. Reward: integration, and a lesson.
burialWindowSay: d41: The village's quarrel was with Werner — and Werner is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
d41: At the grave, Kelly, Sophia, Vasyl and 1 more speak for Ella — "Werner trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
d42: That night, they bring Werner home. Nobody asks you to help carry; nobody has to. By morning the grave is dug by the fire, and the body is laid out beside it. The filling of it is yours.
d44: You say a few words for Werner. Not a ceremony — just: you were here, and someone noticed you leaving. (-3 trauma)
d44: You bury Werner. A marker, of sorts. The village will know where. (+4 trauma)
echoSample: d44: "Werner owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
d48: "Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "Werner always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
d48: "Nobody says Werner's name right yet. We will. Give it a few days."
echoV2Sample: d44: The village raises a marker by the fire — Werner, day 44. a hushwolf. A place to stand.
echoV2DeltaSample: d44: The village raises a marker by the fire — Werner, day 44. a hushwolf. A place to stand.
halfRationLines: d73: "Triage tents and broth for the sick, or half rations till it passes, or the healthy hunt hard to keep everyone fed. Pick — everything costs."
